text.p: This is a summary of spending measures announced by Treasurer Peter Costello in his Tuesday budget for the year to June 30, 1998.
The impact of each measure on the coming four fiscal years is shown, in A$ millions, and the measures are ordered approximately by size. A minus sign indicates higher spending.
NET SPENDING MEASURES
NET SPENDING MEASURES 392 1,766 3,417 4,942
SPENDING CUTS
SAVINGS INCENTIVES. In this, by far the biggest spending cut, the government will replace the former government's superannuation contribution with a cheaper tax break on savings. -1 1,079 2,414 3,980
RENT ASSISTANCE. Removal of a double subsidy.
RURAL ADJUSTMENT SCHEME
FEDERAL-STATE HOUSING DEAL. New funding arrangements.
DRUGS SUBSIDIES. The government is cutting the cost of medical subsidies by paying a fixed amount for each group of therapeutic products (say, anti-depressants).
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY. A rationalisation of the government's computer budget.
CHILDCARE. Limits on new places.
DEFERRED RETIREMENT BONUS. Money for people who defer retirement.
SOCIAL SECURITY CRACKDOWN. More data matching.
HEALTH EFFICIENCIES. Refocussing general practice
PHARMACEUTICALS. Some items dropped from the free list.
CHILDREN'S SERVICES PROGRAMME. Improved targetting.
GOVERNMENT PROPERTY MAINTENANCE. Improved procedures.
TAX CRACKDOWN. More Data matching with social security.
INDUSTRY JOBS SCHEME. Abolished
VOCATIONAL EDUCATION. Grants to states
LOCAL GOVERNMENT FUNDING. Cut.
TOTAL ADDITIONAL SPENDING 391 575 671 768
FEDERATION FUND. A birthday present for the 100th anniversay of the federation of Britain's Australian colonies, in 2001.
OLYMPIC FUNDING. Boosted.
RURAL POLICY PACKAGE 45 46 52 55
AUSTRALIAN FILM FINANCE CORPORATION. Funding continued.
MISCELLANEOUS. Many items, too numerous to itemise.
This list excludes measures announced before the budget.

Also excluded are two items which have been counted as new policy -- the establishment of an environmental fund from the Telstra privatisation proceeds and a commitment to maintain pensions at 25 percent of average adult earnings.
Both of those measures were already budgeted in the government's contingency reserve, which has been adjusted to allow for their formal implementation.
